limitations: Finite-input equivalence to existing student arithmetic, not native quality.
Complete student graph timings exclude D3D12 integration and do not accelerate native NVIDIA execution.
Exact full-image results cover only the checked checkpoints, inputs and environment.
No candidate meets native image quality. Native execution is unchanged.
Twelve new training and four new validation photo identities were selected before captures and fitting. All older validation cases stay excluded from training.
The training budget remains 4500 steps; adding images reduces average exposure per image. One seed does not establish a general limit.
The staged baseline includes 1500 extra feature-pretraining steps; it is not compute-matched to the RGB-only models.
Images are static sample-rendered planes. Earlier DLSS processing resamples their appearance before true 1920x1080 neural inputs are captured.
Only first-reset frames enter training/evaluation. No representative gameplay or temporal quality acceptance is claimed.
Validation scores guide research after evaluation and do not become an independent final test suite. Pixel metrics alone cannot prove preserved perceptual quality.
Existing student fusions are rechecked on the new weights and new inputs; this turn introduces no new execution kernel.
Student graph timings include full 1080p inference and grading, but exclude D3D12 integration and do not accelerate the native runtime.
Every sample launch verifies the exact hidden executable and uses a private inactive desktop. Normal sample state is restored after each trial; game and driver settings are untouched.
